alternatives.question: How can a Venus flytrap respond differently to one touch, two close signals, and continued prey stimulation?
alternatives.whyRetain: Strongest biological rival and independently sufficient. It offers a living transformation, a memorable brain-free memory mechanism and excellent tactile visuals. I select dice narrowly for the more directly reconstructable central evidence: anyone can follow which outcomes win. Flytrap remains a worthy future video, not downgraded for appearing in the owner library or because Frog covered biology. Current source limits constrain detail separately from editorial merit.
limitations: Counting is operational response to electrical signals; do not imply numerals, intentions, consciousness or arithmetic.
Timing/threshold conditions are central: not an unconditional two-touch rule, nor any arbitrary five pokes causing digestion.
Institutional reports inspected; 2016 primary PMC body blocked and 2020/2023 papers not inspected. Full research must resolve exact mechanical touch/AP relationship and biological scope.
2020 source explicitly says later counting pathways remain under investigation; 2023 report is not a license to claim every decoder identified.
No footage, microscopy or fluorophore asset rights cleared.
alternatives.status: reconsiderable; not consumed, queued, excluded or approved

alternatives.question: If every plank is replaced and the old planks build a second ship, which ship is the original?
alternatives.whyRetain: A serious independently sufficient philosophical rival. It earns its payoff by clarifying a question, not by producing another plot twist or a definitive answer. Dice wins for this slot because it lets the viewer resolve the initial challenge through transparent evidence; Theseus requires making the relevance of identity criteria felt rather than merely posing an irresolvable word puzzle. That treatment burden, not philosophy or uncertainty itself, makes my recommendation narrower.
limitations: Thought experiment and philosophical reasoning, not an observed experiment proving identity.
No settled universal solution or automatic extension to personal identity.
Original vessel/history/Plutarch detail not claim-verified; reconstructed voyage is an explicit hypothetical.

alternatives.question: Why do just23 people give better-than-even odds that some pair shares a birthday in the standard model?
alternatives.whyRetain: Independently sufficient, useful and familiar to retell; no penalty for library or early reservoir mention. Dice edges it on pre-answer involvement: a choice feels controllable and then reveals a circular relation, whereas birthdays can be received passively as another surprising number. Birthday has a cleaner single combinatorial insight; its numerical setup and any-pair misunderstanding remain meaningful rivals, not filler.
limitations: Assume independent uniformly distributed birthdays over365 dates; actual birthdays are seasonal and leap days exist.
No guarantee in any room; about50.7%, not exactly50%.
253 pair tests are not mutually independent; do not add253/365 and call it the probability.
No present saturation or audience familiarity measured.

alternatives.question: How did Apollo12 continue after lightning struck it twice during launch?
alternatives.whyRetain: Strongest retained event-story rival; danger and teamwork have a more immediate emotional charge than dice. No penalty for recent history or engineering stories. Dice wins on the ability to make the full key explanation independently visible in a concise demonstration: Apollo needs enough power/telemetry distinction to avoid reducing an exceptional recovery to somebody flipped a switch. Its source access is promising, and this decision does not declare the rescue payoff inferior in principle.
limitations: NASA caption is preliminary institutional account; primary report/transcripts located but uninspected.
No single switch restarted engines or fixed every failure; distinguish readings, power and guidance.
No fabricated dialogue, abort deadline or lone-hero attribution.
Archive licensing and faithful equipment/weather portrayal need later review.

alternatives.question: Why do you not see a hole where your retina has no light receptors?
alternatives.whyRetain: Immediate self relevance and experiential payoff make this independently sufficient. Dice wins here because its evidence can be presented consistently without requiring a viewer to hold a phone at a particular distance with one eye closed. That is presentation reliability, not lower intrinsic merit; an accessible successful personal demonstration could be extremely powerful. Existing person-switch lead concerns a different phenomenon.
limitations: Phone size/distance/eye position changes whether the demonstration works; no guaranteed success or vision diagnosis.
Teaching source’s broad statement about bilateral fields needs nuanced review; do not say your brain recreates an objectively exact lost image.
Detailed filling-in mechanisms need primary literature, not simple AI/inpainting analogy.
